title: Founding cohort — who may sign the ladder into existence, and until when
description:
Governs content/competence/bootstrap-cohort.yaml. Steward-controlled, like proficiency.yaml, and for the same reason: it decides what a credential means.

WHY THIS FILE HAS TO EXIST. The ladder cannot start on its own — L3 requires an L4 signer, L4 requires L5, L5 requires L5 — so decision 43 admits a CLOSED, TIME-LIMITED founding cohort on demonstrated external standing, whose every signature is permanently marked. That was implemented as a field on the credential and nothing else, which left 'closed' and 'time-limited' as adjectives in a document rather than properties of the system: any signer could write `bootstrapAuthority` with a plausible basis string and be a founder, of a cohort that had no roster, no convening, and no closing date. A closed cohort anybody can join is not closed, and a time-limited one with no stated limit does not expire.

WHAT THE ROSTER IS FOR. It converts founding standing from something a credential ASSERTS into something a verifier RESOLVES, offline, against a file a steward signed. The same move the trust registry makes for issuers, and the same move the project made for signer standing in general — a system built to replace 'trust me, he's competent' should not accept 'trust me, I'm a founder'.

SCOPE IS THE CONTROL THAT MATTERS MOST. A founder is admitted on standing in a FIELD: a primary-laboratory appointment in dimensional metrology, an assessor role for a named scope. Bootstrap authority that ran across all 43 domains would let three people mint the entire ladder in a weekend, and it would contradict the project's first principle — no single person should hold all of it. So membership names the domains the member's standing actually covers, and a bootstrap signature outside them is an error rather than a judgement call.

NOT CONVENED IS THE SAFE DEFAULT. A roster with no `closesOn` means no cohort has been convened, and NO bootstrap signature is valid. That is the correct state today: appointing stewards is blocked on people, nothing has issued a credential, and a file that permitted bootstrap signing before anybody had been appointed would be the hole this schema exists to close.

issuedOn.description:
When this roster was cut. THE SAME FIELD THE TRUST REGISTRY CARRIES, AND FOR THE SAME REASON: a verifier resolves this file offline, so everything they conclude from it is a statement about the world as it stood on this date, and an answer that does not carry its own age presents a month-old roster as a current one.

Rule 8b says a verifier resolves this document exactly as they resolve the trust registry. It was not true: the registry had an issue date, a sequence and a place for a signature, and this had none of the three.

sequence.description:
Monotonically increasing roster number, so a verifier holding two copies can tell which is newer and can detect being handed an older one.

THE ROLLBACK THIS CATCHES IS NOT THE REGISTRY'S. A stale registry loses revocations and key compromises. A member is never removed from this roster — there is no field for it — so an older copy can only lack admissions, which is the safe direction. What an older copy CAN carry is a later `closesOn`: a cohort closed early by a steward reopens the moment somebody presents the previous file, and bootstrap signing resumes after the date it was supposed to end. That needs no forgery, only a helpful courier, and the sequence number is what makes it visible.

convenedOn.description: When the cohort was constituted. Absent until a steward convenes it.

closesOn.description:
The last date a bootstrap signature is valid. REQUIRED FOR ANY BOOTSTRAP SIGNATURE TO BE ACCEPTED — its absence means the cohort has not been convened, and the validator refuses every bootstrap signature rather than defaulting to permissive.

'Time-limited' was in the decision from the start and had no mechanism. After this date the ladder must carry itself: by then the cohort has produced holders who can sign as peers, which is the entire point of the exercise. Credentials signed before it stay valid forever and keep their marker — closing the cohort ends new bootstrap signing, it does not un-happen the old.

Extending this date is a steward act with a governance record, not a configuration change. Quietly extending it indefinitely is how a bootstrap becomes a permanent aristocracy.

members.description: The roster. May be empty, which means no cohort has been convened and nobody holds bootstrap authority.

did.description: The member's identifier, matched against `signers[].did` on a credential claiming their authority.

name.description: Optional, and unlike almost everywhere else in this project it is APPROPRIATE here. Minimal PII is a design constraint for credential holders, who are the people the system has power over. A founding-cohort member is exercising that power, and their accountability for it is public by design.

admittedOn.description: A signature dated before this is not covered by the member's authority. Prevents backdating a credential into a period when the signer had no standing.

basis.description: The external standing this member was admitted on — a primary-laboratory or NMI appointment, accreditation assessor status, a publication record. Recorded here as well as on each credential so a reader can compare the two: a credential whose stated basis does not match the roster is asserting something the cohort did not grant.

scope.description: The domains this member's standing covers, and therefore the only domains they may bootstrap-sign in. There is deliberately NO wildcard: a person competent to vouch across all 43 domains is exactly the person the project says should not exist.

maxCredentials.description: Optional ceiling on how many credentials this member may bootstrap-sign in total. The mechanism is here so governance CAN set a volume limit; the number itself is a steward judgement and this schema declines to invent one. Unset means no ceiling, which is honest rather than safe — scope is the control doing the real work.

proof.description:
The roster is itself signed, or it is a text file anybody can edit on the way to the air gap — and the attack is the registry's attack one tier up: ADD A MEMBER, and every credential they bootstrap-sign at L3, L4 and L5 validates. A founding signer is precisely the one who signs WITHOUT holding the level, so this is the highest-privilege signature in the system and it was the less defended of the two documents.

It uses the SAME proof definition as the credentials and the registry, and must: a verifier who can check a credential and the registry it resolves against, but not the roster that granted its signer authority, has checked two of the three documents the answer rests on.

OPTIONAL, FOR THE REASON THE REGISTRY'S PROOF IS OPTIONAL. Signing this is a steward act and no steward has been appointed, so requiring the field would make the project's own shipped roster invalid — which would be resolved by somebody fabricating a proof, the worst available outcome. The gap is made MEASURABLE instead: an unsigned roster is reported wherever a bootstrap claim rests on one, and says what it leaves open.

There is deliberately no `nextExpectedUpdate` beside it. The registry needs one because nothing else bounds how long it may be trusted; this roster carries `closesOn`, after which no bootstrap signature is valid at all, so its staleness is already bounded by a field that does more than measure it.
